answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil floods by requiring every key to post a one-shot cipher at dawn of the epoch: a commitment that binds its public key to the published seed and a unique work artifact. Influence then rises only as the identity climbs a terrace of independent, slashable peer attestations on that same binding. Empty shells can emit commitments cheaply, but they cannot buy the terrace, because established peers will not stake standing on unread clones, and a replayed artifact fails the seed check.
